q: Once registered, an architect's membership in the integrated professional organization (UAP) is:
n: Once registered, an architect automatically becomes a member of the integrated professional organization (the UAP). Source: RA 9266, Sec. 40.

q: What must an agency do before engaging a foreign professional allowed to practice here?
o: Secure a special permit from PRC (and DOLE work permit)
Get a work visa from Immigration only
n: Before engaging a foreign professional allowed to practise here, the agency must secure a PRC special/temporary permit for him, and a DOLE Alien Employment Permit. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 38; Labor Code, Art. 40.

q: What must architects have before performing any service, or be guilty of a misdemeanor?
n: RA 9266 requires architects to have a written contract before performing any service. Practising without one is penalized. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 29.

q: What is the maximum prison term for violating RA 9266?
n: The penal clause provides imprisonment of six months to six years, so the maximum is 6 years. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 29.

q: Which provision must be written into all contract documents an architect prepares?
n: Every contract document the architect prepares must state that the plans and specifications are the architect's property (ownership of plans and specifications). Source: RA 9266, Sec. 33.

q: All architectural plans, designs, specifications, drawings, and architectural documents relative to the construction of a building shall bear the _____ only of an architect registered and licensed under R.A. No. 9266 together with his/her professional identification card number and the date of its expiration.
n: Architectural plans, designs, specifications and documents for a building may bear only the seal and signature of an architect registered and licensed under RA 9266. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 20 and 32.

q: Registration may not be refused, nor a name removed from the roster, on conviction for what kind of offense?
n: Registration may not be refused, nor a name removed from the roster, for conviction of a political offense. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 22.

q: Disputes subject to ______ are settled under the UAP document provisions.
n: Disputes subject to arbitration are settled under the provisions of the UAP documents and CIAC rules. Source: UAP Document 301 (General Conditions); EO 1008.

q: The Architect shall not use nor use self-laudatory, exaggerated, or misleading publicity. However, the presentation of factual materials, verbal or visual, of the aims, standards, and progress of the profession through literature or by industrious application of his work and services which tend to dignify the profession or advance public knowledge of the Architect's function in society may be presented through any public communication media.
n: The Code bars self-laudatory, exaggerated or misleading publicity, but allows factual presentation of the profession's aims, standards and progress. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct (duties to the public).

q: An architect must not solicit free ______ from suppliers when it obligates him against the client's interest.
n: An architect must not solicit free engineering or allied design services from suppliers when that obligates him against the client's interest. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct (duties to manufacturers and suppliers).

q: When the suspension of construction exceeds a period of ____ months, the fee for the remaining works shall be doubled.
n: Under the 2016 Guidelines, if construction is suspended for more than 6 months, the fee for the remaining work is doubled. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202 (other conditions).

q: Which RLA is directly responsible for the total design and assumes civil liability for the documents he signed and sealed?
n: The architect-of-record is directly responsible for the total design and bears civil liability for the documents he signed and sealed. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3 (definitions); RA 9266 IRR.

q: Which RLA is directly responsible and liable for construction supervision?
n: The architect-in-charge of construction is directly responsible and liable for construction supervision. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3 (definitions).

q: Who is the professionally and academically qualified architect with a specialization?
n: A consulting architect is professionally and academically qualified, with exceptional or recognized expertise in a specialized branch of architecture. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3 (definitions).

q: Agroup of professionals in architecture and allied professions, incorporated with architects for the purpose of delivering professional service in architecture and allied professions.
n: An architectural corporation is a group of architects and allied professionals incorporated with the SEC to deliver professional services in architecture and allied fields. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3 (definitions).

q: A juridical entity, synonymous with architectural partnership.
n: An architectural company is a juridical entity synonymous with an architectural partnership. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3 (definitions).

q: Signed and sealed plans and specifications are submitted with the notarized application for a:
n: Signed and sealed plans and specifications are submitted with the notarized application for a building permit. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 302.

q: Which term refers only to a Philippine RLA in good standing with the IAPOA who specializes in a branch of architecture?
n: A Filipino professional consulting architect is a Philippine RLA in good standing with the IAPOA who specializes in a branch of architecture. Source: RA 9266 IRR (definitions).

q: An architectural firm working with a foreign architect forms a:
n: An architectural firm working with a foreign architect on a project forms a consortium or association. Source: RA 9266 IRR (definitions); RA 9266, Sec. 37.

q: What are services rendered by architectural firms or consulting architects called?
n: Services rendered by architectural firms or consulting architects are professional architectural consulting services. Source: RA 9266 IRR (definitions).

q: Architectural corporation duly registered with SEC or a single proprietorship duly registered with DTI, and likewise registered with PRC and BOA to perform state-regulated architectural services.
n: An architectural firm is an architectural corporation registered with the SEC or a sole proprietorship registered with the DTI, also registered with PRC and the Board to perform state-regulated architectural services. Source: RA 9266 IRR (definitions); RA 9266, Sec. 37.

q: Which section of RA 9266 covers ownership of plans, specifications and contract documents?
n: Section 33 of RA 9266 covers ownership of plans, specifications and other contract documents. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 33.

q: Who performs soil investigation on site?
n: A geotechnical engineer (a civil engineer specializing in geotechnics) performs soil investigation and testing on site. Source: NSCP 2015, Chapter 3 (Excavation and Foundations).

q: Under PD 1096, the appointed Building Official must be a registered:
n: Under PD 1096, the Building Official must be a registered architect or civil engineer. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 206.

q: CPD stands for:
n: CPD means Continuing Professional Development. Under RA 10912, professionals earn CPD units through accredited programs to keep their licenses current. Source: RA 10912 (CPD Act of 2016).

q: What is the necessary requirement before practicing architecture?
n: A board passer may practise only after taking the professional oath and being registered. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 17–18.

q: What is conceiving, choosing and developing the type, disposition, arrangement and proportioning of structural elements?
n: Structural conceptualization is conceiving, choosing and developing the type, disposition, arrangement and proportioning of structural elements. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3 (definitions).

q: When was RA 9266 approved?
n: RA 9266 was approved on March 17, 2004. Source: RA 9266 (Architecture Act of 2004), Official Gazette.

q: Which UAP SPP document covers design-build services?
n: UAP SPP Document 207 covers design-build services. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 207.

q: What term means conduct that gravely violates the community's accepted moral standards?
n: Moral turpitude is conduct that gravely violates a community's accepted moral standards. It is a ground for refusing or revoking registration. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 22–23; Black's Law Dictionary.

q: Refers to contracts or arrangements involving the transfer of systematic knowledge for the manufacture of a product.
n: Technology transfer covers contracts or arrangements for transferring systematic knowledge to make a product, apply a process or render a service. Source: RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code), Sec. 4.2.

q: The Architect-in-charge of Construction is responsible to the owner on what matter?
n: The architect-in-charge of construction is responsible to the owner on technical matters: quality, conformance and inspection. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3; 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 204-A.

q: Who submits the five nominees per Board of Architecture position?
n: The integrated accredited professional organization (UAP) submits nominees for each Board position, from which the President appoints. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 4.

q: Under RA 10912, who accredits Continuing Professional Development providers?
n: Under RA 10912, the CPD Council of each profession accredits CPD providers and programs. Source: RA 10912, Sec. 9.
